t.1.178.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those adorned young men wearing earrings, assembled together and vying with one another, each deeming weapon-skill and strength to reside in himself, all sprang up with pride.
t.1.178.3: Eyeing one another in rivalry, their limbs flooded with the passion born of desire, the kings sprang up suddenly from their royal seats, each declaring, "Kṛṣṇā shall be mine!"
t.1.178.2: Swollen with pride in their beauty, their valor, their lineage, their virtue, and their youth, they were like lordly Himālayan elephants in rut, their temples split open by the surging force of musth.
t.1.178.4: Those kṣatriyas, gathered together in the arena and eager to win that daughter of Drupada, shone like the assembled hosts of gods seeking Umā, the daughter of the king of mountains.
t.1.178.5: Those kings, their limbs tormented by the arrows of Kandarpa and their hearts gone out to Kṛṣṇā, having descended into the arena for the sake of Drupada's daughter, there made enemies even of their friends.
t.1.178.6: Then the hosts of the gods came in their celestial chariots: the Rudras and Ādityas, the Vasus and the two Aśvins, all the Sādhyas, and likewise the Maruts, placing Yama and the Lord of Wealth at their head.
t.1.178.7: The Daityas, the Suparṇas and the great serpents, the divine seers, the Guhyakas and the Cāraṇas, Viśvāvasu, Nārada and Parvata, and the chief Gandharvas together with the Apsarases were there.
t.1.178.8: There Halāyudha and Keśava, and the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas, the foremost among them in order of rank, only looked on; those bulls of the Yadus remained steadfast in Kṛṣṇa's counsel.
t.1.178.10: He pointed out to Rāma Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Jiṣṇu, and the two heroic twins; and Rāma, slowly gazing at them one by one, looked at Janārdana with a delighted heart.
t.1.178.9: For when the foremost hero of the Yadus saw them, looking like lordly rutting elephants, like five great elephants with lotus-spotted skin, like fires whose bodies are covered with ash, he pondered deeply about the Pārthas.
t.1.178.12: Likewise those long-armed sons of Pṛthā, and the two heroic twins of great majesty as well, all of them, on beholding Draupadī then, were struck by the arrows of Kandarpa.
t.1.178.13: That place was crowded with divine seers and Gandharvas, frequented by Suparṇas, Nāgas, Asuras and Siddhas, filled with a heavenly fragrance, and strewn with heavenly garlands.
t.1.178.11: But others, sons and grandsons of various kings, their eyes, minds and very natures gone to Kṛṣṇā, straining at the bow with lips bitten and faces flushed copper-red, saw her as if whirling before them.
t.1.178.14: That sky became crowded, filled with great sounds and the roll of kettledrums; on every side it was thronged with celestial chariots and resounded with flutes, lutes and drums.
t.1.178.16: Those kings, exerting their strength, were dragged down by the hard, springing bow; struggling and lying on the surface of the earth, they were seen wretched, their spirits broken.
t.1.178.15: Then, O king, those hosts of kings, one after another, exerting their prowess for the sake of Kṛṣṇā, could not string that sturdy bow, even with all their force.
t.1.178.17: Then the circle of kings was in distress, crying out “alas, alas,” its armlets and earrings crushed and broken by the stiff bow, its longing for Kṛṣṇā turned away.
t.1.178.18: But in that assembly, whose people were in turmoil, when the lords of men had abandoned their boasts, the son of Kuntī, Jiṣṇu, that hero, wished to string that bow and fit an arrow to it.
